Weeknight Miso-Glazed Salmon

Twenty-five minutes, one pan, and a glaze that caramelizes under the broiler while you steam rice. This is the salmon recipe that convinced my household we do not need a midweek delivery habit.

  • Prep: 10 min
  • Cook: 12 min
  • Serves: 4

Ingredients

  • 4 salmon fillets, about 150 g each, skin on or off
  • 3 tablespoons white miso paste
  • 2 tablespoons mirin
  • 1 tablespoon soy sauce
  • 1 teaspoon grated fresh ginger
  • 1 teaspoon toasted sesame oil
  • Steamed rice and sliced scallions, to serve

Method

  1. Whisk the miso, mirin, soy sauce, ginger and sesame oil into a loose glaze. Pat the salmon dry and brush each fillet generously on the flesh side.
  2. Heat a non-stick or well-seasoned pan over medium heat with a film of neutral oil. Lay the fillets in glaze-side up.
  3. Cook 4 minutes until the skin crisps, then slide the pan under a hot broiler for 5–7 minutes, until the glaze bubbles and darkens at the edges.
  4. Rest two minutes off the heat. Serve over rice with scallions and a spoonful of the pan glaze.

Cook's notes

White (shiro) miso is mild and slightly sweet; red miso works but use two tablespoons and add a teaspoon of sugar. If your broiler runs hot, tent the pan loosely with foil after four minutes so the glaze caramelizes without burning.

Leftovers flake beautifully into a quick onigiri filling or a next-day rice bowl with cucumber and a soft egg.

Comments

Aya — Made this Tuesday; swapped in tofu steaks and it still worked.
Darius — The broiler step is non-negotiable. Stovetop alone leaves the glaze raw.
